A mame, dluznij gsme a powinnij slibu- gicze tiemto listern nassym, dobru nassi wieru krzestiansku nadepsa- nemu kniezi opathowi y conuentu klasstera swrchupsaneho nyniei- ssiemu y buducziemu tu swrchupsanu wes se wssim przislussenstwim, czoz kte wsy przislussij tak, iakoz se swrchupisse a gmenuge, kdyz kolowiek my aneb nassij diediczi a buduczij na pomenuti budem, hned na prwe suche dnij, neb na druhe bezelsti, a konecznie na trzetie suche dnij we dczky zemske a w aeta wloziti a zapsati ku prawemu gieh diedicztwij a plnemu panstwij a zprawcze hodne postawiti wedle rzadu a obyczege zemie Czeske czistie bez zmatku wsselikterakeho, tak iakoz zemie Czeska za prawo ma, tak aby swrchupsana wes s platy, s lidmi y se wssim przislussenstwim k tomu boziemu domu a klassteru swrchupsanemu wiecznie przislusseli, drzany a poziwany byli bez nassij a nassich diediczuow ybuduczich wsselikterake przekazky. entries.english:
7 April 1485, Krumau. The brothers Wok and Peter von Rosenberg transfer the village of Sstiedrkow to Abbot Thomas and the convent of Hohenfurt as compensation for the village of Humno.

CCLXXXI. We, Wok and Peter, natural brothers of Rosenberg, declare in this letter to all, publicly and before everyone who sees it or hears it read, that we have made a new fishpond called ‘Posmiechow’ on our estate at Humno. By means of this pond we flooded and submerged one lan of arable land belonging to Zaborzi, together with its rents, grain dues, and other appurtenances. The land belonged to the venerable and devout father in God, Lord Thomas, abbot, and the convent of our monastery of Hohenfurt. We asked the said abbot and brethren to consent to receive suitable compensation from us, and they graciously agreed. The compensation is the village called Sstiedrkow, in our Rosenberg lordship, where there are three farmsteads with people and rents. We have transferred the said village, with its rents and rent-paying inhabitants, arable and non-arable land, meadows, scrubland, pastures, common lands, boundaries, and all appurtenances belonging to the village and its inhabitants, as it has traditionally lain within its boundaries, to the said abbot, the present and future convent, and their heirs in full and rightful possession. We and our heirs and successors shall retain no right or reservation in it. We undertake by this letter, in good Christian faith, to enter and record the village with all its appurtenances in the land tables and books of the realm, at the first, second, or, at the latest, third court day after being summoned, and to establish it securely in their rightful inheritance and full possession according to the law and custom of Bohemia, without any dispute, so that the village, its rents, inhabitants, and appurtenances may belong to the monastery forever, held and enjoyed without hindrance from us or our heirs and successors. In confirmation, we have voluntarily ordered our seals attached to this letter. Given and written at Krumau on the Thursday after Easter in the year 1485.

Two fairly large, almost identical seals hang from parchment strips, in red wax. Each shows a shield with a rose and a helmet above it, again with a rose; the seals bear the names Wok and Peter von Rosenberg.

CCLXXXII. 12 February 1487. Settlement between Abbot Thomas of Hohenfurt and the monastery’s subjects of Plaben on one side and the citizen of Budweis Mathias Ramschisl on the other, concerning a newly made pond and a watercourse. An amicable settlement was reached concerning the dispute that had arisen between the venerable Lord Thomas, abbot of Hohenfurt, and his people from Plaben on one side, and the prudent citizen Mathias Ramschisl of Budweis on the other, about the construction of a new pond. Mathias shall make and repair a road over the dam on both sides wherever his boundaries indicate, at his own expense and labor, for himself and his successors. He and his successors shall widen the new ditch he made in his meadows so that runoff water can flow freely without obstruction. If, however, by God’s will the river should rise and force the runoff water back through the ditch, this shall cause Mathias and his successors no liability. The old watercourse used previously, now obstructed by the new pond, shall thereafter cease to flow, and no dispute shall arise over it. The people of the abbot of Plaben shall clear the watercourses on their own land so that water can drain away from their holdings. Those present at the settlement were the venerable Abbot Thomas, his brethren Lords Sixtus and Bartholomew, and the noble, prudent burgraves Peter of Dobrohostie, burgrave at Krumau; Oldrich of Dvorce, then burgrave at Welesin; Jan of Dube, then burgrave at Rosenberg; Willem of Trebomyslice; Jan Czimspan of Herslak; Gira na Rynku; Girzik; Jan Prinzer; Sstiopan of Ceske ulice; Pavel Judenrichter; Prokop Ssten; Hanuss Plob; Petr Klemar; Martin Tuczny; Jan Khoczenczagel; Augustin and Rzehorz Ramsislowe; and the prudent citizens of Krumau Mathiass z Wewarzij, Gira Petrltk, Pawel Hoch, Petr Skopecz, reeve in Swiuech, and Jan, reeve of Kaplicka. At the request of the honorable mayor and council and the whole city of Budweis, the city’s large seal was attached to this letter as testimony, without prejudice to the city or its inhabitants. At the request of the mayor and council and the whole city of Budweis, the city’s large seal was attached as testimony, without prejudice to the city or its inhabitants. Given and written on the Monday before Saint Valentine’s Day in 1487.

A fairly large seal of the city of Budweis hangs from a parchment strip in red wax, bearing the city’s arms and a helmet with a royal crown.
